content: 1. Glomerular Filtration and NSAIDs: High-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs can impair glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, potentially increasing the toxicity of tenofovir DF. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. Close monitoring is recommended when co-administering tenofovir DF with ketorolac, as both drugs can increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. 2. Tenofovir DF and Lamivudine: Co-administration of tenofovir DF and lamivudine increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Lartorectinib and Doravirine: Lartorectinib increases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, but caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Lasmiditan and Tenofovir DF: Lasmiditan increases tenofovir DF levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition and other mechanisms. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Lasmiditan inhibits BCRP in vitro, and co-administration with BCRP substrates should be avoided. 5. Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir and Tenofovir DF: This combination increases tenofovir DF levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and other unspecified mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Lenacapavir and Doravirine: Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, increases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Lenacapavir may also increase the risk of adverse reactions for CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose. 7. Leniolisib and Tenofovir DF: Leniolisib, a BCRP inhibitor, increases systemic exposure to BCRP substrates, including tenofovir DF. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 8. Tenofovir DF and Letermovir: Tenofovir DF decreases letermovir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Letermovir co-administration with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 9. Levoketoconazole and Doravirine: Levoketoconazole increases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, but caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Lonafarnib and Tenofovir DF: Lonafarnib, a weak P-gp inhibitor, increases tenofovir DF levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for adverse reactions, and reduce the dose of P-gp substrates if needed. 11. Lopinavir and Doravirine: Lopinavir increases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Lorlatinib and Doravirine: Lorlatinib decreases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Doravirine and Lovotibeglogene Autotemcel: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period. ARTs may interfere with lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing. 14. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor and Doravirine: Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. 15. Mavorixafor and Tenofovir DF: Mavorixafor, a P-gp inhibitor, increases tenofovir DF levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Tenofovir DF and NSAIDs (e.g., Meloxicam, Naproxen): Co-administration of tenofovir DF with NSAIDs increases the risk of toxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered, and therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 17. Tenofovir DF and Metformin: Tenofovir DF increases metformin levels by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of lactic acidosis. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Tenofovir DF and Morphine: Tenofovir DF increases morphine levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Mitomycin and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Mitomycin also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Mitotane and Doravirine: Mitotane decreases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. 21. Neomycin PO and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Neomycin also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Nevirapine and Doravirine: Nevirapine decreases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. 23. Nintedanib and Tenofovir DF: Tenofovir DF decreases nintedanib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 24. Orlistat and Tenofovir DF: Orlistat decreases tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if increased HIV viral load is confirmed. 25. Oxaliplatin and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Oxaliplatin may also increase tenofovir DF levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Oxcarbazepine and Doravirine: Oxcarbazepine decreases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. 27. Pamidronate and Tenofovir DF: Pamidronate increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of nephrotoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Paromomycin and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Paromomycin also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Peginterferon Alfa-2a/2b and Lamivudine: Co-administration increases the risk of liver decompensation due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Pemetrexed and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Pemetrexed also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Pentamidine and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Pentamidine may also increase tenofovir DF levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Pentobarbital and Doravirine: Pentobarbital decreases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. 33. Peramivir and Tenofovir DF: Tenofovir DF increases peramivir levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely, especially when co-administered with nephrotoxic drugs. 34. Phenobarbital and Doravirine: Phenobarbital decreases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. 35. Phenytoin and Doravirine: Phenytoin decreases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine.
